content.comment_body: In my situation, the COM port does not appear in the dropdown menu, even though the driver for the adapter is already installed.

Could you provide more details? What model of [product_name] do you have? Which cable type are you using—USB or RS232 on your PC? If using RS232, what kind of USB/RS232 adapter is used? Also, what is your operating system? Are you able to capture a screenshot showing the issue?

I have a [product_name] with [article_no]. I'm using a serial cable and a USB/RS232 adapter purchased locally, with the driver installed on my laptop. My operating system is Windows 7. There is no error message; the issue is that the COM port does not show up when attempting to connect to [product_name]. Only a virtual Ethernet adapter is displayed as a communication option; the COM port is missing.
Is your cable an original from [company_name] or is it a third-party version?

analysis.insight_summary: Users are facing an issue where the COM port is absent in the dropdown selection when trying to connect to a [product_name], despite installing the required USB/RS232 adapter driver. A lack of error messages complicates troubleshooting, and uncertainty regarding cable compatibility and drivers further adds to the problem.
analysis.user_expectations: Users anticipate that after installing the correct driver, the software should recognize and display the COM port for the USB/RS232 adapter, enabling easy communication with the [product_name].
